title: 1946 Craig Machine Shop had its beginnings by Woodford Craig. Note Town Hall on the right
description: In April 1946, Washington Craig received a building permit for a machine shop. By June of that year, he and his son, Woodford Craig, opened a service station. In 1947, the Craigs were recognized for their generosity when they welcomed hundreds of children to their service station, where Santa Claus greeted them beside a Christmas tree. Each child received a well-filled sack and a special gift. Pastors from various churches led a Christmas service, and Lorne Britton directed the carolling. Residents contributed to a Christmas fund, and after expenses, the remaining funds were donated to the NB Orphanage in Saint John. By 1949, the Craigs had expanded their business to include the sale of cars and farm machinery. In 1952, they began selling v-ploughs and two-wing snowploughs, eventually securing a government contract.
